_about: The character, in words. Pasted into every strip prompt, so a new strip is the same boy. Edit here, not in prompts.
name: sprite boy
description: a 12-year-old boy: short spiky black hair, warm tan skin, simple friendly face with small dark eyes, athletic but slim build. Bright cyan-blue sleeveless tank top, red athletic shorts, white ankle socks, blue sneakers with white laces and soles. Clean cartoon video-game illustration: confident medium-weight black outline, flat cel shading with one soft shadow tone, vivid saturated colors, high detail, crisp edges
locked: Blue sneakers. No green shoes (author decision, 2026-11-19).
Clothing as in the original Grok sprites.
Proportions locked to the master character sheet (Charles, 2026-11-21).
No shadows on sprites. A keyed-out drawn shadow made him look like he was floating; the contact shadow is a composite-time layer (config/scene.json, contact-shadow) (Charles, 2026-11-21).
view: side-on body with the head and shoulders turned about 30 to 45 degrees toward the camera, so most of his face (both eyes) and a little of his chest show, facing right, with the SAME angle in every pose
far_side: Draw the arm and leg on the far side of the body in a SLIGHTLY darker shade of the SAME color, only about 10% darker (skin a little deeper, shorts a little deeper red, shoe a little deeper blue), the same hue as the near side, never brown, grey or near-black, so near and far limbs can be told apart without looking dirty or shadowed.
background: perfectly flat solid magenta (#FF00FF), nothing else. No ground shadow, no floor line, no scenery, no gradient, no text, labels, numbers or arrows.
view_note: Author preference (2026-11-20): the look of the chart 2 push-up and the ChatGPT chart 3 sheets: the body is side-on so the motion is clear, but the head and shoulders turn toward the camera so the face and a little of the chest show. Chart 1 strips were made in strict side view and their prompts keep that wording. Use the same angle in every pose of a strip, and in every figure on a multi-row sheet, or the pose change shows a jump in the turn (the crossfade, now retired, showed it as a ghost).
body_rules: BODY AND FACE RULES (every figure): exactly TWO arms and TWO legs, so count the limbs in every figure before you finish and never draw a third arm or leg; loose red athletic shorts that hang to mid-thigh with a wide leg opening, clearly shorts and not tights, leggings or briefs; a calm, friendly face with a small closed smile and level eyebrows, the eyes looking where he is going: no smirk, no big grin, no raised cheek; the back straight in standing and crouching poses; feet relaxed and natural, never pointed like a ballet dancer; PROPORTIONS LOCKED to the master character sheet: the same head size, head-to-body ratio, limb lengths, hand and shoe size and build in every figure and every strip, so a lying figure is the same boy as a standing one; NO cast shadow or ground shadow under or beside the figure (a contact shadow is added later, at composite time, on its own layer).
far_side_note: Charles (2026-11-21): some takes overdid the far-side shading until it read as a dark shadow. Ask for light shading, about 10% darker with the hue matched. Existing sheets are fixed by a one-time recolor saved as a new asset version, not a redo and not a runtime mask.
